title: A mutual perpetual chase entered by a quiet Black move is still a draw

boundary.expect: second occurrence; not yet a draw by mutual violation

rationale: The mirror of mx-mix-005: the same mx-mix-002 wheel, entered by a quiet move from the other side. Black's king steps c6c7, which captures nothing, gives no check, and leaves both attack configurations exactly as they stood — the black cannon on b5 is attacked from b1 before and after it, the white cannon on f3 from f7 — so the entry renews no chase; the repeating position, which is mx-mix-002's own start position, then stands on the board at plies 1, 5 and 9. Strictly inside that window each of White's four moves shuttles the horse between c5 and b3 and switches the attacker on the unprotected black cannon b5 between b1 and e5, and each of Black's four moves shuttles the horse between e3 and f5 and switches the attacker on the unprotected white cannon f3 between f7 and c3, so every move of both sides renews the chase of one and the same undefended target and neither side ever gives check. The mutual rule therefore makes this a draw carrying the reserved reason mutual-perpetual-chase. Patch-gated against fork correction P3: the current unpatched engine also intersects the chase set of the quiet entry move, which empties the last mover's accumulator, and returns a unilateral loss for Red — the side that did not enter — so this fixture states the contract against the engine and is expected to fail until that correction lands. Its reason identifier is separately gated on the fork accessor exposing which repetition branch fired, exactly as for mx-mix-002. Reviewed as a pair with mx-mix-005, this fixture is what shows the defect hands the win to whichever side made the entry move: one and the same wheel, one and the same set of judged moves, and the unpatched engine names the other side the loser each time.
